Definition: (adverbially) in front of; usually (with other particles) on account of, so as, since, hence
BiblicalUsage: In front of is the word for standing before the king: I know of certainty that ye would gain the time, because ye see the thing is gone from me; Daniel went in unto Arioch and said, destroy not the wise men of Babylon, bring me in before the king; and thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image.
TheologicalSignificance: I take the standing before as the place of the test, where the wise men fail and Daniel stands.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
